provenance: PR #25 R2 (MEDIUM, repair): verifier-aggregate-superlative-fails-loud pins only the no-ground-truth FAIL direction; nothing proved the comment's own claim that expect.answer still decides the L2 path on its own merits. Row 1 is the reviewer's exact repro (no expect -- fails loud, the declared D22 ceiling). Row 2 is the missing direction: the same task text, the same superlative phrasing, but with expect.answer supplied -- verify()'s has_ground_truth gate means aggregate_needs_comparison never even runs, so answers_match alone decides it, and it PASSes. Row 3 guards against a shallow fix that made the guard silently skip itself whenever expect is present regardless of correctness -- a wrong ground-truth answer must still fail, just for the ordinary L2 reason.

triage.note: tagged invariant: the claim in verifier.py's own comment ('answers_match still decides them on their own merits') was uncited and unguarded -- the same species of defect as R1's dangling support-matrix citation, just inside code instead of docs. Watched red first as an 'unknown verifier probe(s)' error, since _run_verifier_case had no 'aggregate' key until this PR. M31 appended rows 4 and 5: the guard now relaxes on a trace carrying a GRADED `extract_all` step -- the comparison primitive the guard's own comment said the plan vocabulary lacked -- and row 5 pins that a superseded one, dropped by an act-ladder replan, does not count. Each was watched red against the variant it exists to rule out: row 4 against the pre-M31 guard (no relaxation at all) -- should_pass true, verdict FAIL; row 5 against a relaxation written over `trace` instead of `graded` -- should_pass false, verdict PASS.
